subject.title: Update to 2026.7.1 left managed install and WhatsApp plugin linked to old embedded Node

question: Should a managed `openclaw update` automatically hand off embedded-Node replacement to the openclaw.ai installer, or fail before mutation and require a separately invoked installer recovery flow?
rationale: The observable bug is clear, but the permanent fix determines cross-repository ownership, download trust, rollback behavior, and whether the updater may rewrite managed launch and shell entrypoints.

options.title: Atomic installer handoff
options.body: Have the updater invoke a versioned, verified installer protocol that replaces the managed Node and core roots, repairs service/plugin links, validates readiness, and rolls back as one transaction.

options.title: Fail before mutation
options.body: Detect an unsupported managed Node before changing core state and present a visible installer repair action that completes the upgrade outside the running updater.

options.title: Document manual recovery
options.body: Keep updater and installer independent and rely on terminal recovery instructions, accepting continued release-blocking friction for managed users.

recommendation.title: Atomic installer handoff
recommendation.body: Have the updater invoke a versioned, verified installer protocol that replaces the managed Node and core roots, repairs service/plugin links, validates readiness, and rolls back as one transaction.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is the earlier canonical managed-install and dual-root repair work in the installer repository.
